why: The canonical build-from-traversals problem: preorder tells you which value is the root, inorder tells you which values go to its left and which to its right. Recursing on those two ranges rebuilds the tree.
hints: Where is the root in preorder? Once you know the root, what does its position in inorder tell you?
Everything left of the root in inorder is its left subtree and everything right is its right subtree. The left subtree's values come next in preorder, then the right subtree's.
Map value -> inorder index. Recurse build(lo, hi) on inorder ranges while consuming preorder with one moving index: root first, then build left, then right. O(n).
pitfalls: Searching inorder for the root at every step is O(n^2); the index map makes it O(n).
Build the left subtree before the right one, because that is the order preorder lists them.
Values are not in BST order; do not compare them, look up their inorder positions.
A skewed tree of 1000 nodes recurses 1000 deep: raise Python's recursion limit.
